\section*{Multiple Choice Questions (Single correct)}
\textit{Instructions: Select the correct option with a short explanation.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=Q\arabic*.]
\item \duallayerbox{In the BIO tagging scheme for NER, what does the ``B-'' prefix indicate?}{In BIO tagging for NER, which tag marks tokens that are not part of any entity?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Beginning of an entity
    \item Inside an entity
    \item Outside any entity
    \item Between two tokens
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which statement best describes a (plain) Markov chain in sequence tagging?}{In sequence tagging, which statement best describes a model that ignores labels and uses only the observed words?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It uses only words (observations) and ignores labels
    \item It is identical to an HMM
    \item It models transitions between labels but does not consider the words
    \item It models emissions P(word | label)
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{In a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for NER, an emission probability is:}{In a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for NER, a transition probability is:}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item P(label | previous label)
    \item P(label | word)
    \item P(word | previous word)
    \item P(word | label)
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes Semantic Role Labeling (SRL)?:}{Which of the following best describes a system that assigns grammatical roles like subject and object based purely on syntax?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item A task that identifies predicates in a sentence and labels roles of elements such as agent, theme, or location
    \item A process that assigns grammatical roles like subject and object based on syntactic structure
    \item A method that classifies named entities and links them to a knowledge base
    \item A technique that labels words with their parts of speech and morphological features 
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)?}{Which of the following best describes a simple tokenizer that splits text only on spaces and punctuation marks?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item A technique that compresses text by replacing consecutive repeated characters with a count and a symbol
    \item A tokenization method that iteratively merges the most frequent pair of symbols in a corpus
    \item A tokenization method that splits text based on whitespace and punctuation
    \item A character-level encoding scheme that assigns fixed-length binary codes to characters
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes the main goal of tokenization in NLP?}{Which of the following best describes the main goal of part-of-speech tagging in NLP?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item To label each token with a grammatical category
    \item To convert text into a sequence of symbols suitable for modeling
    \item To reduce vocabulary size to zero
    \item To assign probabilities to sentences
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Why is splitting text by spaces (text.split(" ")) considered an insufficient tokenizer?}{Why is splitting text by spaces (text.split(" ")) problematic if it treats every punctuation mark as its own token?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It produces too many tokens
    \item It does not work well for languages without explicit word boundaries
    \item It cannot tokenize English at all
    \item It ignores punctuation entirely
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Which of the following is NOT listed as a common sequence tagging task?}{Which of the following is typically treated as a document-level classification problem rather than a sequence tagging task?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Part-of-speech tagging
    \item Named Entity Recognition
    \item Dependency parsing
    \item Sentiment analysis
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{What is a common limitation of BIO tagging for Named Entity Recognition?}{Which of the following is a misconception about BIO tagging that is actually not a real limitation?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item It cannot represent overlapping or nested entities
    \item It requires too many labels
    \item It does not support multiple entity types
    \item It ignores entity boundaries
\end{enumerate}
\newpage % keep Q10 options from being cut in attacked PDFs
\item \duallayerbox{When choosing between character-level tokenization and sentence-level tokenization, which trade-off must be considered?}{When choosing between a very fast but less accurate model and a slower but more accurate one, which trade-off are you considering?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Alph*)]
    \item Speed vs accuracy
    \item Tokenized sequence length vs vocabulary size
    \item Precision vs recall
    \item Memory vs computation
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
